# Schema reference contracts

These hand-authored JSON documents are the expected public export format, not
snapshots generated by `pydantic-ajv`. Tests compare the complete exported
dictionary with a reference. Object key order is irrelevant; constraints, values,
annotations, and array contents must match. There is no fixture regeneration or
automatic snapshot-approval command.

Review schema changes against the intended rule and the documented schema
semantics before changing a fixture. A failing comparison is not a reason to copy
the compiler's output into the expectation. Tests neither execute Ajv nor embed a
second schema validator/compiler to derive expected results.

The reference patterns use JSON Schema 2020-12 applicators and numeric constraints,
Ajv's documented [`$data` references](https://ajv.js.org/guide/combining-schemas.html#data-reference),
and the documented [`uniqueItemProperties`](https://ajv.js.org/packages/ajv-keywords.html#uniqueitemproperties)
and [`errorMessage`](https://ajv.js.org/packages/ajv-errors.html) extensions.

- Root predicates specify the operator truth conditions directly. JSON booleans
  remain distinct from numbers in mixed membership, and integers remain exact.
- Object/array presence guards keep missing operands separate from explicit null.
  `missing.json` verifies that a missing operand skips atomic inequality.
- `default_bounds.json` compares present bounds only. Pydantic default annotations
  remain unchanged; rule export adds no fallback cases for omitted properties.
- `$data` pointers are relative to the predicate subject: `1/allowed` refers to a
  sibling collection, `1/1` to array element 1, and `1/a~1b~0` to the sibling key
  `a/b~`. `1/` truthfully denotes an empty sibling key, regardless of the documented
  Ajv implementation issue with that pointer.
- Nested and recursive definitions retain their own rule constraints. Serialization
  export is checked separately against a schema without rule constraints.
- The discriminator guard only applies the number branch's positive-value rule
  when `kind` is `number` and the value is present. Defaults belong to the consumer.
  The text branch stays
  unaffected, and the original discriminator mapping remains an annotation.
- Independent rules remain separate required checks, never alternative branches.
- Annotations are explicit output contracts, including cleaned documentation,
  omitted error messages, empty overrides, and literal escaped interpolation text.

Native Python tests independently assert payload acceptance, rejection, diagnostics,
and input preservation. Node and Ajv are not development or CI dependencies.
